# Assessment submission 

**Title:** Traceback-Based Bug Classification for Automated Python Repair

**Domain:** Machine Learning

**Abstract:** This project investigates traceback-based classification of Python bugs and its use in a test-verified repair workflow. Labelled examples are generated by injecting six known mutation categories into working Python programs and capturing the resulting failures. TF-IDF features are used to train and compare Naive Bayes, logistic regression, SVM, random forest and AdaBoost. Models are selected using validation macro F1 and evaluated on held-out mutation families using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and confusion matrices, with majority and exception-name baselines. PCA provides an exploratory visualization. The selected classifier guides repair strategies; proposed code is accepted only after independent tests pass. A local web interface supports classification, evaluation and repair demonstrations. Results are limited to a controlled synthetic benchmark; real-world generalization and the benefit of classification-guided repair require further evaluation.

**Problem statement:** Python exception names identify an error category but may not uniquely identify the underlying programming mistake. Developers must inspect traceback context and program behavior to diagnose failures. This project explores whether a supervised classifier can provide useful bug-category predictions and use those predictions to structure repair attempts. Independent test execution provides a practical acceptance check, although it does not prove correctness. Existing repair tools may already classify or verify fixes; the project makes no claim that these capabilities are absent from current tooling.

**Tools:** Python 3.11+, scikit-learn, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, joblib, FastAPI, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, pytest, Docker, subprocess, ast, optional Gemini REST API, dotenv, Git and GitHub Actions. PCA is for visualization; classifiers use nonnegative TF-IDF directly.

**Applications:** Educational feedback and controlled failure-triage experiments. The CLI can support a first-pass CI triage workflow, with developer review of proposed changes. Production deployment, real-world classification accuracy and automatic repair of arbitrary repositories are outside the demonstrated scope.
